title: The Memory Witness: A Simulated Investigation
instructions: 阅读下面的文章，回答10个问题。文章为模拟教学材料，非真实事件。问题类型包括单选、填空、匹配和判断正误/未提及。填空题答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。请先阅读全文，再作答。
passage:
A small town library in the north of England recently hosted a weekly memory workshop for older residents. The project, called 'Recall and Reason', was designed by a local psychologist, Dr. Helen Marsh, to study how people remember everyday events. Its findings offer a fascinating insight into the way human memory actually works, and they carry important lessons for both everyday life and the legal system.

As part of the study, participants were asked to describe a short film they had watched together. The film showed a man walking into a café, ordering coffee, and leaving a newspaper on a table. After a week, the participants were asked to write down what they remembered. Dr. Marsh was surprised by the results. Most people remembered the main actions correctly, but many added details that were not in the film at all. For example, one woman insisted that the man had been wearing a hat, although he had not. Another participant claimed that the café had a red door, but the door was actually blue.

Dr. Marsh explained that these errors are entirely normal. 'Our brains fill in gaps with what we expect to see,' she said. 'This is not lying; it is how memory works.' In other words, memory is not a perfect recording of events but an active reconstruction, shaped by our knowledge, expectations and past experience. When a detail is missing, the mind often supplies a plausible substitute without our being aware of it.

The workshop then focused on the difference between confident memories and accurate memories. Dr. Marsh showed that people who were very confident about a detail were often wrong. This finding has important implications for legal testimony. In court, witnesses are often asked to recall events months or years later, by which time their memories may have changed considerably. If confident witnesses can be mistaken, judges and juries must be careful. Dr. Marsh suggested that police interviews should be recorded and that witnesses should be asked open questions first, so that their own account is not shaped by the interviewer's suggestions. She also recommended that line-ups should be conducted fairly, with similar-looking people, to avoid unfair identification.

The project ended with a public talk. Many residents said they now understood why they sometimes misremember. One man said, 'I used to think I had a bad memory, but now I know it's just normal.' Dr. Marsh hopes to run a larger study next year, with younger participants as well. She believes that understanding memory errors can help everyone, not just witnesses. 'If we know how memory fails,' she said, 'we can design better systems for justice and for everyday life.'

grammar.title: 复合句与简单句搭配；条件、让步和原因表达；标点
grammar.explanation: 英语中，简单句只有一个主谓结构，而复合句包含两个或多个主谓结构，通过连词连接。条件句常用 if 引导，表示假设；让步句常用 although, though, even though 引导，表示转折；原因句常用 because, since, as 引导，表示原因。标点方面，当从句位于主句之前时，通常用逗号隔开；位于主句之后时，一般不用逗号。例如：'If we know how memory fails, we can design better systems.' 中，if 从句在前，用逗号；'She believes that understanding memory errors can help everyone.' 中，that 从句在后，不用逗号。
grammar.example: If we know how memory fails, we can design better systems for justice and for everyday life.
